venture.name: Collarbone Protective Sports Undershirt
venture.name_status: Descriptive working name from Venture Workspace; brand not specified
venture.concept: Compression sports undershirt with padding focused on the clavicle
venture.target_customers: Male and female contact-sport athletes ages 12-30, especially hockey players and athletes with prior injuries
venture.customer_needs: Comfortable fit, stable pad placement, freedom of movement, and credible value for money
venture.value_proposition: Proposed affordable, low-bulk clavicle cushioning under sports equipment; effectiveness remains untested
venture.geographic_market: Global ambition, primarily United States and Canada
venture.distribution_channels: Not specified. Direct online sales, Amazon, and team partnerships are strategic options, not established channels
venture.features: Clavicle-focused pad placement and compression fit; male and female versions contemplated; removable versus fixed padding undecided
venture.source: Luke Ryan(1).pdf, supplied Venture Workspace, read in full
venture.prior_research_limits: Reported Amazon sample was not supplied for audit. AI focus-group responses are simulated, not human willingness-to-pay evidence. Injury statistics and prevention claims are not independently established by this pricing study.

comparison.scope: Descriptive category comparison only: P01, P03, P04, one representative per brand. Different coverage and sports; not equivalent protection or confirmed in-stock choices. USD per shirt before tax/delivery.

direct_comparison.note: Only one explicitly clavicle-padded direct benchmark; no robust direct-market distribution can be inferred.

preliminary_recommendation.rationale: Test a focused clavicle design above the $44.99 targeted sternum shirt and below Unequal’s $99.95 hockey shirt and $119.95 clavicle-padded shirt. The $49 prior workspace hypothesis is a test point, not validated willingness to pay. Broader-coverage products do not justify a premium automatically.
preliminary_recommendation.conditions: Confirm materials, manufacturing, testing, fulfillment, returns and channel margin; test actual customer demand and fit. Canadian pricing requires separate CAD and landed-cost work.

market_opportunities: Interpretation: A focused $49-$69 design could offer a lower entry price than multi-area Unequal shirts if testing and costs support it.
Interpretation: Offer clear coverage diagrams, accurate sizing and a feasible size-exchange policy to reduce purchase uncertainty.
Hypothesis: Test fit across male/female and youth/adult athletes under hockey equipment; do not assume a universal cut works.
Hypothesis: Compare fixed and removable pads for stability, washing and durability before choosing.
Hypothesis: Test a two-shirt practice/game bundle or team order offer only after margins are known.
Verified correction: Existing Invincible clavicle pads contradict the workspace claim that no shirt has collarbone pads.
research_limitations: Five selected offers from three brands are not a census of the market.
Prices were observed on official pages on 2026-10-27; they may change and were not confirmed at checkout.
Verified means the listed price was observed, not that all sizes are available or performance claims are proven.
G-Form availability is ambiguous. A displayed comparison price does not prove a historic selling price.
US USD prices only; Canadian pricing, taxes, delivery and duties not researched.
Padding coverage and intended sports differ. Category statistics are descriptive, not an equivalent-protection price index.
No independent evidence here establishes fracture prevention or validates the venture’s injury statistics.
Costs, demand, manufacturing feasibility, willingness to pay and finalized distribution channels remain unknown.
The supplied focus group is simulated and the reported consumer-review sample was not provided for verification.
missing_value_policy: null means no separate reliable value established; never zero
